# Anvil, Grindstone & Gear Progression

## Context

The game shipped XP + an **Enchanting Table** (4 enchantments, applied to the selected
hotbar item) and Hardcore mode. The natural completion of that progression arc is gear
*maintenance and consolidation*: a way to repair worn gear, merge enchantments, rename
items, auto-repair from XP, and strip enchantments back for a refund. This plan adds:

- **Anvil** — repair worn gear two ways (same-item **combine**, which also merges
  enchantments; and **material repair**, consuming the gear's tier material), plus
  **rename**. Costs XP levels.
- **Grindstone** — strip all enchantments off an item, refunding some XP.
- **Mending** enchantment — applied at the *existing* Enchanting Table; passively
  diverts gained XP to repair the held/worn gear that carries it.
- **Save format v11** — adds an optional per-slot `customName` (rename); Mending rides
  the existing per-slot `enchantments`.

This makes the XP/enchanting loop matter long-term, follows the zero-asset principle
(new blocks are procedurally painted, sounds reuse existing synth), and stays inside the
engine's established idioms.

## Key architecture facts (verified)

- **Stations are not slot machines.** Furnace/brewing/villager are recipe-book filters
  (`Recipe.station`, `lib/game/types.ts:72`); the Enchanting Table operates on the
  **selected hotbar slot** (`InventoryPanel.tsx:233`, `EnchantingColumn.tsx`). There is
  **no transient working-slot state**. The Anvil and Grindstone follow the
  selected-hotbar-slot idiom — no new persistent/transient item slots, so no dupe/loss
  surface. (Durable gear is always `count:1`, so combine/strip can't split a stack.)
- **Two distinct `craftingStation` unions.** The engine/UI union (`"furnace" |
  "villager" | "brewing" | "enchanting" | null`) lives in **four** places —
  `GameState.craftingStation`, `GameSnapshot.craftingStation`, the `openedStation` event
  (all in `lib/game/engine/state.ts`), and the `InventoryPanel` prop
  (`InventoryPanel.tsx:22`). `"anvil"` and `"grindstone"` are added to those four and
  **not** to `Recipe.station`. `STATION_LABELS` (`InventoryPanel.tsx:41`, keyed off
  `Recipe.station`) therefore needs no change.
- **Compile-enforced exhaustive maps** (a missing entry is a `tsc` error, not a silent
  bug): `GROUP_BY_BLOCK` in `lib/game/audio/materials.ts` (new blocks),
  `ENCHANTMENT_DEFS` in `enchantments.ts` + `VALID_ENCHANT_IDS` in `save.ts:180`
  (the `mending` id). `BLOCK_COLORS` in `lib/world/blocks.ts` sizes the texture atlas —
  a new block **must** have an entry or it samples garbage UVs.
- **`awardXp` (`lib/game/engine/systems/xp.ts:37`) is the single XP-bank seam**, called
  from mob kill (`GameEngine.ts`), fishing (`fishing.ts`), and ore mining
  (`mining.ts`). Mending plugs in here, once.
- **Save migration chain** (`save.ts:154-165`) extends to v11 by the same additive
  pattern used for v7→v10; `restoreSlot` (`save.ts:205-221`) is the one place to restore
  `customName`, inside its durable-gear block.
- **No `WORLDGEN_VERSION` bump.** Anvil/Grindstone are craft-only and never emitted by
  worldgen (exactly like Furnace/Chest/BrewingStand/EnchantingTable); a new enum id at
  the end shifts no existing terrain or saved diff.

## Design decisions (from clarifications)

- **Repair = both models.** The Anvil offers (a) **same-item combine** — merge a second
  unit of the same item: durability = sum + a small bonus, capped; enchantments = union
  at the higher per-id level; and (b) **material repair** — consume one unit of the
  gear's tier material to restore a fixed % of max durability (no enchant change). Plus
  **rename**.
- **Grindstone included** — strips all enchantments off the selected item and refunds XP
  scaled to the total levels removed.
- Mending is **binary** (`maxLevel: 1`). Rename and `customName` are **durable-gear
  only** (avoids the stackable-merge identity hazard). Combine/repair refuse no-ops so XP
  and materials are never silently burned.

---

## Implementation

### 1. Two new blocks — `Anvil`, `Grindstone`

- `lib/world/blocks.ts`: add `Anvil` and `Grindstone` to the `BlockId` enum (after
  `EnchantingTable`); add `HELD_BLOCK_COLORS` + **`BLOCK_COLORS`** entries (dark iron
  tones) for each.
- `lib/world/atlas.ts`: add a painter branch in `drawTile` for each — a dark metal base
  with a lighter top face band (mirror the EnchantingTable branch). No new constants; the
  atlas loop already covers new ids once `BLOCK_COLORS` includes them.
- `lib/game/audio/materials.ts`: add `[BlockId.Anvil]: "stone"` and
  `[BlockId.Grindstone]: "stone"` to `GROUP_BY_BLOCK` (**mandatory** — exhaustive Record).
- `lib/game/items.ts`: add `BREAK_HARDNESS` entries; item defs `{ id:"anvil",
  kind:"block", blockId:BlockId.Anvil }` and the grindstone equivalent; `BLOCK_TO_SLOT`
  entries.
- `lib/game/recipes.ts`: add two `CRAFTING_RECIPES` (both land in "Building" via
  `recipeCategory`):
  - `anvil`: `3 gold_ore + 4 cobble → anvil`
  - `grindstone`: `2 cobble + 2 planks → grindstone`

A new solid block needs no other registration (meshing/lighting/`isSolid` default to
opaque cube). *Recipe costs are tunable — flag in review if a different gating is wanted.*

### 2. Open the stations — `lib/game/engine/systems/interact.ts`

Extend `InteractiveKind` with `"anvil" | "grindstone"`; add both to `INTERACTIVE_BLOCKS`;
add `tryInteractBlock` branches; add `interactAnvil` / `interactGrindstone` handlers
mirroring `interactEnchantingTable` (`interact.ts:157`) — each sets `inventoryOpen=true`,
`craftingStation=<id>`, emits `openedStation`. The `openedStation` consumer
(`useMinecraftGame.ts`) is station-agnostic, so pointer-lock release needs no extra wiring.

### 3. Thread the station ids — `lib/game/engine/state.ts`

Add `"anvil" | "grindstone"` to `GameState.craftingStation`, `GameSnapshot.craftingStation`,
and the `openedStation.station` event union. Add one-shot events:
`anvilCombined | anvilRepaired | anvilRenamed | grindstoneStripped` to `GameEvent`.

### 4. Mending enchantment — `types.ts`, `enchantments.ts`, `config.ts`, `xp.ts`

- `types.ts:17`: `EnchantmentId = ... | "mending"`.
- `config.ts` (near enchant tunables): `MENDING_MAX_LEVEL = 1`,
  `MENDING_REPAIR_PER_XP = 2`.
- `enchantments.ts`: add the `mending` def (`kinds:["tool","weapon","armor"]`,
  `maxLevel: MENDING_MAX_LEVEL`) to `ENCHANTMENT_DEFS`; append to `ENCHANTMENT_ORDER`.
  Add the **single Mending seam reader** (analog of `unbreakingSkips`):

  ```ts
  // Diverts gained XP to repair damaged Mending gear (held item first, then equipped
  // armor in ARMOR_SLOTS order). Returns a (possibly new) slots array + XP left to bank.
  export function mendXp(slots, selectedSlot, equipped, xp): { slots; xpLeft }
  ```

  Repairs `MENDING_REPAIR_PER_XP` durability per diverted XP point, never above
  `maxDurability`; clones slots only on first write; returns the same ref + full `xpLeft`
  when no Mending gear is present (back-compat). Imports `ARMOR_SLOTS`/`EquippedArmor`
  from `items.ts` (safe — no cycle; must **not** import `inventory.ts`).
- `xp.ts:37`: in `awardXp`, run `mendXp` first, bank `xpLeft`, but still
  `emit({type:"xpGained", amount})` with the **gross** amount so HUD/audio react. No
  cycle (`enchantments.ts` doesn't import `xp.ts`).

Mending is applied at the **existing Enchanting Table** via the unchanged `enchant`
command + `applyEnchant`/`canEnchant` (which already gate by `def.kinds` and cap at
`maxLevel`).

### 5. `customName` + save v11 — `types.ts`, `save.ts`, `GameEngine.ts`

- `types.ts`: add `customName?: string` to `InventorySlot` and `SavedSlot`. Rename the
  current v10 shape to `SaveDataV10` and define `SaveData` as `version: 11`.
- `save.ts`: add `"mending": true` to `VALID_ENCHANT_IDS` (**mandatory**);
  include `customName` in `inventorySlotsSnapshot`; restore it inside `restoreSlot`'s
  **durable-gear block** (trim + cap to `ANVIL_NAME_MAX_LEN`, drop if empty); add
  `migrateSaveV10toV11` (pure bump) and chain it in `readSave` (extend the parse/migrate
  unions, change the final guard to `!== 11`).
- `GameEngine.ts` `serialize()`: return `version: 11`.

### 6. Pure logic — `lib/game/anvil.ts` (new), `lib/game/grindstone.ts` (new), `items.ts`, `config.ts`

`config.ts` (after the enchant block):
```ts
ANVIL_COMBINE_COST_LEVELS = 4    // same-item combine (merges enchants)
ANVIL_REPAIR_COST_LEVELS  = 1    // material repair
ANVIL_RENAME_COST_LEVELS  = 1
ANVIL_REPAIR_BONUS_PCT    = 0.12 // bonus durability on combine
ANVIL_MATERIAL_REPAIR_PCT = 0.25 // durability restored per material unit
ANVIL_NAME_MAX_LEN        = 32
GRINDSTONE_REFUND_XP_PER_LEVEL = 5 // XP points refunded per enchant level stripped
```

`items.ts` — `REPAIR_MATERIAL_BY_ITEM: Record<string,string>` mapping each gear id to its
tier material, derived from each item's crafting recipe (confirm ids against
`recipes.ts`). Pattern: `wood_* → planks`, `stone_* → cobble`, `sliver_* → sliver_ore`,
`ruby_* → ruby_ore`, `gold_* → gold_ore`, `sapphire_* → sapphire_ore`,
`diamond_* → diamond_ore`, armor → its base material (e.g. `leather`), `bow`/`fishing_rod
→ string`. Gear with no entry simply has the material-repair action hidden (combine still
works). Also add a shared `displayName(slot) = slot.customName ?? slot.label` helper.

`lib/game/anvil.ts` (pure; imports types + `ENCHANTMENT_DEFS` + config — no engine/state):
- `mergeEnchantments(a, b)` — per-id max level, each capped at its def `maxLevel`.
- `findSacrificeIndex(slots, selectedSlot)` — index of another slot with the same durable
  id (`count>0`), else -1.
- `wouldCombineHelp(target, sacrifice)` — true iff durability would rise or an enchant
  added/raised (no-op guard).
- `combineSlots(target, sacrifice)` — durability = `min(max, tDur + sDur +
  floor(max*BONUS))`; enchants = `mergeEnchantments`.
- `materialRepair(slot)` — durability = `min(max, dur + ceil(max*MATERIAL_REPAIR_PCT))`;
  `canMaterialRepair(slot, inventory)` checks `REPAIR_MATERIAL_BY_ITEM` + a unit in stock
  + not already full.
- `sanitizeCustomName(raw)` — trim + cap to `ANVIL_NAME_MAX_LEN`.

`lib/game/grindstone.ts` (pure):
- `enchantRefund(slot)` — total levels × `GRINDSTONE_REFUND_XP_PER_LEVEL`.
- `stripEnchantments(slot)` — returns slot with `enchantments` undefined.

### 7. Commands — `commands.ts`, `GameEngine.ts`

Add to the `Command` union: `anvilCombine`, `anvilRepair`, `anvilRename {name}`,
`grindstoneStrip`. Add handlers after the `enchant` case, each gating on
`!isDead && canInteract(gameMode) && craftingStation === <station>` and operating on
`inventory[selectedSlot]`:
- **anvilCombine**: require a durable target + `findSacrificeIndex ≥ 0` +
  `wouldCombineHelp`; spend `ANVIL_COMBINE_COST_LEVELS`; write `combineSlots` to the
  target, `createEmptySlot()` to the sacrifice. (Net item count strictly −1.)
- **anvilRepair**: require `canMaterialRepair`; spend `ANVIL_REPAIR_COST_LEVELS`; consume
  one material unit (existing inventory-decrement helper); write `materialRepair`.
- **anvilRename**: durable only; sanitize; refuse no-op; spend `ANVIL_RENAME_COST_LEVELS`;
  set/clear `customName`.
- **grindstoneStrip**: require enchanted durable item; bank `enchantRefund` via the XP
  seam (`state.xp += refund`); write `stripEnchantments`.

All spend XP only after every guard passes (`spendXpLevels` is all-or-nothing), emit the
matching one-shot event.

### 8. UI — `AnvilColumn.tsx` + `GrindstoneColumn.tsx` (new), wiring

- `components/game/AnvilColumn.tsx` — mirror `EnchantingColumn.tsx`. Operates on the
  selected hotbar item; hint when it isn't durable gear. Three actions: **Combine**
  (enabled iff a helpful sacrifice exists + enough XP; status text mirrors enchanting),
  **Repair** (enabled iff `canMaterialRepair` + enough XP; shows the material + current
  `dur/max`), **Rename** (controlled input seeded from `customName`, re-keyed on
  slot/selection; enabled iff changed + enough XP). Imports the pure `anvil.ts` helpers.
- `components/game/GrindstoneColumn.tsx` — selected item, a Strip button (enabled iff it
  has enchantments) showing the XP refund preview.
- `components/game/InventoryPanel.tsx` — add `"anvil" | "grindstone"` to the prop union
  and the new callback/cost props; add two branches before the `enchanting` branch
  (`InventoryPanel.tsx:232`).
- `lib/game/useMinecraftGame.ts` — expose `anvilCombine/anvilRepair/anvilRename/
  grindstoneStrip` dispatchers.
- `components/game/MinecraftGame.tsx` — destructure them, import the cost constants, pass
  through to `InventoryPanel`.
- **Label propagation**: replace `slot.label` with `displayName(slot)` in
  `ItemTooltip.tsx` (`itemTooltipFor`), `Hotbar.tsx` (selected label), `InventoryPanel`
  aria-labels, and `EnchantingColumn`/the new columns so a renamed item shows everywhere.
- `app/ui.css` — add `.anvil-column` / `.grindstone-column` / `.anvil-rename-field` /
  action-button styles by copying the `.enchanting-column` / `.enchant-entry` rules. Pure
  CSS, zero assets.
- *(Optional)* `lib/game/audio/audioDirector.ts` — play existing procedural
  enchant/XP sounds on the new events (the switch has no `default`, so this is additive
  and never breaks the build).

---

## Tests

Mirror existing patterns; all must stay green in `bun test`:
- `lib/game/anvil.test.ts` (new) — `mergeEnchantments`, `findSacrificeIndex`,
  `wouldCombineHelp`, `combineSlots` (sum+bonus capped, immutable, enchant union),
  `materialRepair`/`canMaterialRepair`, `sanitizeCustomName`.
- `lib/game/grindstone.test.ts` (new) — `enchantRefund`, `stripEnchantments`.
- `lib/game/enchantments.test.ts` — extend: `canEnchant(... ,"mending")` for
  tool/weapon/armor; `mendXp` repairs held then armor, respects `xpLeft`, never exceeds
  max, and is a no-op (same ref) without Mending gear.
- `lib/game/engine/systems/xp.test.ts` — `awardXp` diverts XP to a damaged Mending item

# Anvil, Grindstone & Gear Progression

## Context

The game shipped XP + an **Enchanting Table** (4 enchantments, applied to the selected
hotbar item) and Hardcore mode. The natural completion of that progression arc is gear
*maintenance and consolidation*: a way to repair worn gear, merge enchantments, rename
items, auto-repair from XP, and strip enchantments back for a refund. This plan adds:

- **Anvil** — repair worn gear two ways (same-item **combine**, which also merges
  enchantments; and **material repair**, consuming the gear's tier material), plus
  **rename**. Costs XP levels.
- **Grindstone** — strip all enchantments off an item, refunding some XP.
- **Mending** enchantment — applied at the *existing* Enchanting Table; passively
  diverts gained XP to repair the held/worn gear that carries it.
- **Save format v11** — adds an optional per-slot `customName` (rename); Mending rides
  the existing per-slot `enchantments`.

This makes the XP/enchanting loop matter long-term, follows the zero-asset principle
(new blocks are procedurally painted, sounds reuse existing synth), and stays inside the
engine's established idioms.

## Key architecture facts (verified)

- **Stations are not slot machines.** Furnace/brewing/villager are recipe-book filters
  (`Recipe.station`, `lib/game/types.ts:72`); the Enchanting Table operates on the
  **selected hotbar slot** (`InventoryPanel.tsx:233`, `EnchantingColumn.tsx`). There is
  **no transient working-slot state**. The Anvil and Grindstone follow the
  selected-hotbar-slot idiom — no new persistent/transient item slots, so no dupe/loss
  surface. (Durable gear is always `count:1`, so combine/strip can't split a stack.)
- **Two distinct `craftingStation` unions.** The engine/UI union (`"furnace" |
  "villager" | "brewing" | "enchanting" | null`) lives in **four** places —
  `GameState.craftingStation`, `GameSnapshot.craftingStation`, the `openedStation` event
  (all in `lib/game/engine/state.ts`), and the `InventoryPanel` prop
  (`InventoryPanel.tsx:22`). `"anvil"` and `"grindstone"` are added to those four and
  **not** to `Recipe.station`. `STATION_LABELS` (`InventoryPanel.tsx:41`, keyed off
  `Recipe.station`) therefore needs no change.
- **Compile-enforced exhaustive maps** (a missing entry is a `tsc` error, not a silent
  bug): `GROUP_BY_BLOCK` in `lib/game/audio/materials.ts` (new blocks),
  `ENCHANTMENT_DEFS` in `enchantments.ts` + `VALID_ENCHANT_IDS` in `save.ts:180`
  (the `mending` id). `BLOCK_COLORS` in `lib/world/blocks.ts` sizes the texture atlas —
  a new block **must** have an entry or it samples garbage UVs.
- **`awardXp` (`lib/game/engine/systems/xp.ts:37`) is the single XP-bank seam**, called
  from mob kill (`GameEngine.ts`), fishing (`fishing.ts`), and ore mining
  (`mining.ts`). Mending plugs in here, once.
- **Save migration chain** (`save.ts:154-165`) extends to v11 by the same additive
  pattern used for v7→v10; `restoreSlot` (`save.ts:205-221`) is the one place to restore
  `customName`, inside its durable-gear block.
- **No `WORLDGEN_VERSION` bump.** Anvil/Grindstone are craft-only and never emitted by
  worldgen (exactly like Furnace/Chest/BrewingStand/EnchantingTable); a new enum id at
  the end shifts no existing terrain or saved diff.

## Design decisions (from clarifications)

- **Repair = both models.** The Anvil offers (a) **same-item combine** — merge a second
  unit of the same item: durability = sum + a small bonus, capped; enchantments = union
  at the higher per-id level; and (b) **material repair** — consume one unit of the
  gear's tier material to restore a fixed % of max durability (no enchant change). Plus
  **rename**.
- **Grindstone included** — strips all enchantments off the selected item and refunds XP
  scaled to the total levels removed.
- Mending is **binary** (`maxLevel: 1`). Rename and `customName` are **durable-gear
  only** (avoids the stackable-merge identity hazard). Combine/repair refuse no-ops so XP
  and materials are never silently burned.

# Anvil, Grindstone & Gear Progression

## Context

The game shipped XP + an **Enchanting Table** (4 enchantments, applied to the selected
hotbar item) and Hardcore mode. The natural completion of that progression arc is gear
*maintenance and consolidation*: a way to repair worn gear, merge enchantments, rename
items, auto-repair from XP, and strip enchantments back for a refund. This plan adds:

- **Anvil** — repair worn gear two ways (same-item **combine**, which also merges
  enchantments; and **material repair**, consuming the gear's tier material), plus
  **rename**. Costs XP levels.
- **Grindstone** — strip all enchantments off an item, refunding some XP.
- **Mending** enchantment — applied at the *existing* Enchanting Table; passively
  diverts gained XP to repair the held/worn gear that carries it.
- **Save format v11** — adds an optional per-slot `customName` (rename); Mending rides
  the existing per-slot `enchantments`.

This makes the XP/enchanting loop matter long-term, follows the zero-asset principle
(new blocks are procedurally painted, sounds reuse existing synth), and stays inside the
engine's established idioms.

## Key architecture facts (verified)

- **Stations are not slot machines.** Furnace/brewing/villager are recipe-book filters
  (`Recipe.station`, `lib/game/types.ts:72`); the Enchanting Table operates on the
  **selected hotbar slot** (`InventoryPanel.tsx:233`, `EnchantingColumn.tsx`). There is
  **no transient working-slot state**. The Anvil and Grindstone follow the
  selected-hotbar-slot idiom — no new persistent/transient item slots, so no dupe/loss
  surface. (Durable gear is always `count:1`, so combine/strip can't split a stack.)
- **Two distinct `craftingStation` unions.** The engine/UI union (`"furnace" |
  "villager" | "brewing" | "enchanting" | null`) lives in **four** places —
  `GameState.craftingStation`, `GameSnapshot.craftingStation`, the `openedStation` event
  (all in `lib/game/engine/state.ts`), and the `InventoryPanel` prop
  (`InventoryPanel.tsx:22`). `"anvil"` and `"grindstone"` are added to those four and
  **not** to `Recipe.station`. `STATION_LABELS` (`InventoryPanel.tsx:41`, keyed off
  `Recipe.station`) therefore needs no change.
- **Compile-enforced exhaustive maps** (a missing entry is a `tsc` error, not a silent
  bug): `GROUP_BY_BLOCK` in `lib/game/audio/materials.ts` (new blocks),
  `ENCHANTMENT_DEFS` in `enchantments.ts` + `VALID_ENCHANT_IDS` in `save.ts:180`
  (the `mending` id). `BLOCK_COLORS` in `lib/world/blocks.ts` sizes the texture atlas —
  a new block **must** have an entry or it samples garbage UVs.
- **`awardXp` (`lib/game/engine/systems/xp.ts:37`) is the single XP-bank seam**, called
  from mob kill (`GameEngine.ts`), fishing (`fishing.ts`), and ore mining
  (`mining.ts`). Mending plugs in here, once.
- **Save migration chain** (`save.ts:154-165`) extends to v11 by the same additive
  pattern used for v7→v10; `restoreSlot` (`save.ts:205-221`) is the one place to restore
  `customName`, inside its durable-gear block.
- **No `WORLDGEN_VERSION` bump.** Anvil/Grindstone are craft-only and never emitted by
  worldgen (exactly like Furnace/Chest/BrewingStand/EnchantingTable); a new enum id at
  the end shifts no existing terrain or saved diff.

## Design decisions (from clarifications)

- **Repair = both models.** The Anvil offers (a) **same-item combine** — merge a second
  unit of the same item: durability = sum + a small bonus, capped; enchantments = union
  at the higher per-id level; and (b) **material repair** — consume one unit of the
  gear's tier material to restore a fixed % of max durability (no enchant change). Plus
  **rename**.
- **Grindstone included** — strips all enchantments off the selected item and refunds XP
  scaled to the total levels removed.
- Mending is **binary** (`maxLevel: 1`). Rename and `customName` are **durable-gear
  only** (avoids the stackable-merge identity hazard). Combine/repair refuse no-ops so XP
  and materials are never silently burned.

---

## Implementation

### 1. Two new blocks — `Anvil`, `Grindstone`

- `lib/world/blocks.ts`: add `Anvil` and `Grindstone` to the `BlockId` enum (after
  `EnchantingTable`); add `HELD_BLOCK_COLORS` + **`BLOCK_COLORS`** entries (dark iron
  tones) for each.
- `lib/world/atlas.ts`: add a painter branch in `drawTile` for each — a dark metal base
  with a lighter top face band (mirror the EnchantingTable branch). No new constants; the
  atlas loop already covers new ids once `BLOCK_COLORS` includes them.
- `lib/game/audio/materials.ts`: add `[BlockId.Anvil]: "stone"` and
  `[BlockId.Grindstone]: "stone"` to `GROUP_BY_BLOCK` (**mandatory** — exhaustive Record).
- `lib/game/items.ts`: add `BREAK_HARDNESS` entries; item defs `{ id:"anvil",
  kind:"block", blockId:BlockId.Anvil }` and the grindstone equivalent; `BLOCK_TO_SLOT`
  entries.
- `lib/game/recipes.ts`: add two `CRAFTING_RECIPES` (both land in "Building" via
  `recipeCategory`):
  - `anvil`: `3 gold_ore + 4 cobble → anvil`
  - `grindstone`: `2 cobble + 2 planks → grindstone`

A new solid block needs no other registration (meshing/lighting/`isSolid` default to
opaque cube). *Recipe costs are tunable — flag in review if a different gating is wanted.*

### 2. Open the stations — `lib/game/engine/systems/interact.ts`

Extend `InteractiveKind` with `"anvil" | "grindstone"`; add both to `INTERACTIVE_BLOCKS`;
add `tryInteractBlock` branches; add `interactAnvil` / `interactGrindstone` handlers
mirroring `interactEnchantingTable` (`interact.ts:157`) — each sets `inventoryOpen=true`,
`craftingStation=<id>`, emits `openedStation`. The `openedStation` consumer
(`useMinecraftGame.ts`) is station-agnostic, so pointer-lock release needs no extra wiring.

### 3. Thread the station ids — `lib/game/engine/state.ts`

Add `"anvil" | "grindstone"` to `GameState.craftingStation`, `GameSnapshot.craftingStation`,
and the `openedStation.station` event union. Add one-shot events:
`anvilCombined | anvilRepaired | anvilRenamed | grindstoneStripped` to `GameEvent`.

### 4. Mending enchantment — `types.ts`, `enchantments.ts`, `config.ts`, `xp.ts`

- `types.ts:17`: `EnchantmentId = ... | "mending"`.
- `config.ts` (near enchant tunables): `MENDING_MAX_LEVEL = 1`,
  `MENDING_REPAIR_PER_XP = 2`.
- `enchantments.ts`: add the `mending` def (`kinds:["tool","weapon","armor"]`,
  `maxLevel: MENDING_MAX_LEVEL`) to `ENCHANTMENT_DEFS`; append to `ENCHANTMENT_ORDER`.
  Add the **single Mending seam reader** (analog of `unbreakingSkips`):

  ```ts
  // Diverts gained XP to repair damaged Mending gear (held item first, then equipped
  // armor in ARMOR_SLOTS order). Returns a (possibly new) slots array + XP left to bank.
  export function mendXp(slots, selectedSlot, equipped, xp): { slots; xpLeft }
  ```

  Repairs `MENDING_REPAIR_PER_XP` durability per diverted XP point, never above
  `maxDurability`; clones slots only on first write; returns the same ref + full `xpLeft`
  when no Mending gear is present (back-compat). Imports `ARMOR_SLOTS`/`EquippedArmor`
  from `items.ts` (safe — no cycle; must **not** import `inventory.ts`).
- `xp.ts:37`: in `awardXp`, run `mendXp` first, bank `xpLeft`, but still
  `emit({type:"xpGained", amount})` with the **gross** amount so HUD/audio react. No
  cycle (`enchantments.ts` doesn't import `xp.ts`).

Mending is applied at the **existing Enchanting Table** via the unchanged `enchant`
command + `applyEnchant`/`canEnchant` (which already gate by `def.kinds` and cap at
`maxLevel`).

### 5. `customName` + save v11 — `types.ts`, `save.ts`, `GameEngine.ts`

- `types.ts`: add `customName?: string` to `InventorySlot` and `SavedSlot`. Rename the
  current v10 shape to `SaveDataV10` and define `SaveData` as `version: 11`.
- `save.ts`: add `"mending": true` to `VALID_ENCHANT_IDS` (**mandatory**);
  include `customName` in `inventorySlotsSnapshot`; restore it inside `restoreSlot`'s
  **durable-gear block** (trim + cap to `ANVIL_NAME_MAX_LEN`, drop if empty); add
  `migrateSaveV10toV11` (pure bump) and chain it in `readSave` (extend the parse/migrate
  unions, change the final guard to `!== 11`).
- `GameEngine.ts` `serialize()`: return `version: 11`.

### 6. Pure logic — `lib/game/anvil.ts` (new), `lib/game/grindstone.ts` (new), `items.ts`, `config.ts`

`config.ts` (after the enchant block):
```ts
ANVIL_COMBINE_COST_LEVELS = 4    // same-item combine (merges enchants)
ANVIL_REPAIR_COST_LEVELS  = 1    // material repair
ANVIL_RENAME_COST_LEVELS  = 1
ANVIL_REPAIR_BONUS_PCT    = 0.12 // bonus durability on combine
ANVIL_MATERIAL_REPAIR_PCT = 0.25 // durability restored per material unit
ANVIL_NAME_MAX_LEN        = 32
GRINDSTONE_REFUND_XP_PER_LEVEL = 5 // XP points refunded per enchant level stripped
```

`items.ts` — `REPAIR_MATERIAL_BY_ITEM: Record<string,string>` mapping each gear id to its
tier material, derived from each item's crafting recipe (confirm ids against
`recipes.ts`). Pattern: `wood_* → planks`, `stone_* → cobble`, `sliver_* → sliver_ore`,
`ruby_* → ruby_ore`, `gold_* → gold_ore`, `sapphire_* → sapphire_ore`,
`diamond_* → diamond_ore`, armor → its base material (e.g. `leather`), `bow`/`fishing_rod
→ string`. Gear with no entry simply has the material-repair action hidden (combine still
works). Also add a shared `displayName(slot) = slot.customName ?? slot.label` helper.

`lib/game/anvil.ts` (pure; imports types + `ENCHANTMENT_DEFS` + config — no engine/state):
- `mergeEnchantments(a, b)` — per-id max level, each capped at its def `maxLevel`.
- `findSacrificeIndex(slots, selectedSlot)` — index of another slot with the same durable
  id (`count>0`), else -1.
- `wouldCombineHelp(target, sacrifice)` — true iff durability would rise or an enchant
  added/raised (no-op guard).
- `combineSlots(target, sacrifice)` — durability = `min(max, tDur + sDur +
  floor(max*BONUS))`; enchants = `mergeEnchantments`.
- `materialRepair(slot)` — durability = `min(max, dur + ceil(max*MATERIAL_REPAIR_PCT))`;
  `canMaterialRepair(slot, inventory)` checks `REPAIR_MATERIAL_BY_ITEM` + a unit in stock
  + not already full.
- `sanitizeCustomName(raw)` — trim + cap to `ANVIL_NAME_MAX_LEN`.

`lib/game/grindstone.ts` (pure):
- `enchantRefund(slot)` — total levels × `GRINDSTONE_REFUND_XP_PER_LEVEL`.
- `stripEnchantments(slot)` — returns slot with `enchantments` undefined.

### 7. Commands — `commands.ts`, `GameEngine.ts`

Add to the `Command` union: `anvilCombine`, `anvilRepair`, `anvilRename {name}`,
`grindstoneStrip`. Add handlers after the `enchant` case, each gating on
`!isDead && canInteract(gameMode) && craftingStation === <station>` and operating on
`inventory[selectedSlot]`:
- **anvilCombine**: require a durable target + `findSacrificeIndex ≥ 0` +
  `wouldCombineHelp`; spend `ANVIL_COMBINE_COST_LEVELS`; write `combineSlots` to the
  target, `createEmptySlot()` to the sacrifice. (Net item count strictly −1.)
- **anvilRepair**: require `canMaterialRepair`; spend `ANVIL_REPAIR_COST_LEVELS`; consume
  one material unit (existing inventory-decrement helper); write `materialRepair`.
- **anvilRename**: durable only; sanitize; refuse no-op; spend `ANVIL_RENAME_COST_LEVELS`;
  set/clear `customName`.
- **grindstoneStrip**: require enchanted durable item; bank `enchantRefund` via the XP
  seam (`state.xp += refund`); write `stripEnchantments`.

All spend XP only after every guard passes (`spendXpLevels` is all-or-nothing), emit the
matching one-shot event.

### 8. UI — `AnvilColumn.tsx` + `GrindstoneColumn.tsx` (new), wiring

- `components/game/AnvilColumn.tsx` — mirror `EnchantingColumn.tsx`. Operates on the
  selected hotbar item; hint when it isn't durable gear. Three actions: **Combine**
  (enabled iff a helpful sacrifice exists + enough XP; status text mirrors enchanting),
  **Repair** (enabled iff `canMaterialRepair` + enough XP; shows the material + current
  `dur/max`), **Rename** (controlled input seeded from `customName`, re-keyed on
  slot/selection; enabled iff changed + enough XP). Imports the pure `anvil.ts` helpers.
- `components/game/GrindstoneColumn.tsx` — selected item, a Strip button (enabled iff it
  has enchantments) showing the XP refund preview.
- `components/game/InventoryPanel.tsx` — add `"anvil" | "grindstone"` to the prop union
  and the new callback/cost props; add two branches before the `enchanting` branch
  (`InventoryPanel.tsx:232`).
- `lib/game/useMinecraftGame.ts` — expose `anvilCombine/anvilRepair/anvilRename/
  grindstoneStrip` dispatchers.
- `components/game/MinecraftGame.tsx` — destructure them, import the cost constants, pass
  through to `InventoryPanel`.
- **Label propagation**: replace `slot.label` with `displayName(slot)` in
  `ItemTooltip.tsx` (`itemTooltipFor`), `Hotbar.tsx` (selected label), `InventoryPanel`
  aria-labels, and `EnchantingColumn`/the new columns so a renamed item shows everywhere.
- `app/ui.css` — add `.anvil-column` / `.grindstone-column` / `.anvil-rename-field` /
  action-button styles by copying the `.enchanting-column` / `.enchant-entry` rules. Pure
  CSS, zero assets.
- *(Optional)* `lib/game/audio/audioDirector.ts` — play existing procedural
  enchant/XP sounds on the new events (the switch has no `default`, so this is additive
  and never breaks the build).

---

## Tests

Mirror existing patterns; all must stay green in `bun test`:
- `lib/game/anvil.test.ts` (new) — `mergeEnchantments`, `findSacrificeIndex`,
  `wouldCombineHelp`, `combineSlots` (sum+bonus capped, immutable, enchant union),
  `materialRepair`/`canMaterialRepair`, `sanitizeCustomName`.
- `lib/game/grindstone.test.ts` (new) — `enchantRefund`, `stripEnchantments`.
- `lib/game/enchantments.test.ts` — extend: `canEnchant(... ,"mending")` for
  tool/weapon/armor; `mendXp` repairs held then armor, respects `xpLeft`, never exceeds
  max, and is a no-op (same ref) without Mending gear.
- `lib/game/engine/systems/xp.test.ts` — `awardXp` diverts XP to a damaged Mending item
  and banks the remainder; unchanged behavior without Mending gear (existing assertions
  stay green).
- `lib/game/engine/GameEngine.test.ts` — open Anvil/Grindstone (event + station set);
  combine/repair/rename/strip happy paths + refusals (wrong station, no sacrifice/material,
  no-op, too poor → no XP spent, no item loss); **item-count conservation** on combine.
- `lib/game/save.test.ts` — v10→v11 pure bump; `readSave` chains an old save to 11;
  round-trips `customName` on durable gear; trims/caps a bogus name; non-durable drops it.
  Update existing fixtures asserting the final version to 11.
- `lib/game/recipes.test.ts` — anvil + grindstone recipes exist, land in Building, use
  only real item ids.
- `components/game/AnvilColumn.test.tsx` + `GrindstoneColumn.test.tsx` (new) — mirror
  `EnchantingColumn.test.tsx` (hint/enable/disable states, callbacks fire).
- `components/game/InventoryPanel.test.tsx` — add new required props to defaults; assert
  the new columns render for their stations.

## Docs (ship with the change, per AGENTS.md)

- `docs/manual.md` — Anvil (craft, repair/combine/rename) + Grindstone + Mending sections.
- `docs/reference.md` — Anvil/Grindstone blocks, recipes, Mending enchant row, new
  commands/events.
- `docs/tuning.md` — all new `ANVIL_*`, `MENDING_*`, `GRINDSTONE_*` tunables.
- `docs/save-format.md` — v11: `SavedSlot.customName` (additive, durable gear); Mending
  rides existing `enchantments`; pure v10→v11 migration.
- `docs/adding-content.md` — Anvil/Grindstone as the worked example of a craft-only
  interactive block (the exhaustive-map + station-union threading checklist).
- `CHANGELOG.md` — new entry.

## Branch & commits

Big multi-system feature → its own branch off `main`, landing as focused commits, then
one PR against `hutusi/main` (per AGENTS.md). Each commit stays green on
lint/typecheck/test (bisectable) and ships its own docs + tests. Conventional commit
subjects with a "why" body; **no `Co-Authored-By` trailers**.

Branch: `feat/anvil-grindstone-mending`

1. `feat(enchanting): add Mending enchantment` — `mending` id/def, `mendXp` seam +
   `awardXp` wiring, config, tests, manual/reference/tuning docs. Self-contained; no save
   bump (rides existing `enchantments`).
2. `feat(save): bump save format to v11 with per-item custom names` — `customName` on
   `InventorySlot`/`SavedSlot`, v10→v11 migration, restore/sanitize, save tests. Additive
   and green on its own.
3. `feat(anvil): add Anvil for repair, combine, and renaming gear` — block + atlas +
   items + recipe, station wiring, `anvil.ts`, commands/handlers, `AnvilColumn` UI +
   `displayName` propagation, tests, docs, CHANGELOG. Consumes v11 `customName`.
4. `feat(grindstone): add Grindstone to strip enchantments for XP` — block,
   `grindstone.ts`, command/handler, `GrindstoneColumn` UI, station wiring, tests, docs.

Pushing and opening the PR are user-authorized: commit locally, leave review/push to the
user.

## Verification

1. `bun run lint && bun run typecheck && bun run format:check && bun test && bun run build`
   (CI's `verify` gate). The exhaustive-Record and station-union compile checks catch any
   missed wiring during `typecheck`.
2. `bun run test:e2e` — touches the renderer/React shell (new blocks + panels).
3. Manual pass (`bun run dev`): craft an Anvil + Grindstone; right-click each opens its
   panel. With a damaged enchanted sword + a duplicate, Combine restores durability and
   merges enchants for XP; Repair with the tier material restores durability; Rename sets
   a name visible in tooltip/hotbar. Enchant Mending at the Enchanting Table, then mine
   ore and watch held-gear durability climb as XP is gained. Grindstone strips enchants
   and refunds XP. Save, reload — `customName`, enchantments, and durability persist; an
   older (v10) world still loads.

## Risks & mitigations

- **Item dupe/loss** — durable gear is `count:1`; combine clears the sacrifice and
  rewrites the target in one new array after XP is charged (net −1, asserted by test).
  Material repair decrements one material unit via the existing helper.
- **`customName` + stacking** — rename + restore are durable-only, so renamed items never
  hit the id-based stack-merge path. The single biggest reason to keep rename durable-only.
- **Two `craftingStation` unions** — add the new ids to the four engine/UI sites, not to
  `Recipe.station`; a miss is a `tsc` error.
- **Exhaustive-Record gates** — `GROUP_BY_BLOCK` (2 blocks), `ENCHANTMENT_DEFS` +
  `VALID_ENCHANT_IDS` (`mending`) must be updated or the build fails (guardrails, listed).
- **Save migration** — v10→v11 is a pure bump; `customName` is optional and sanitized on
  restore; update v10 fixtures' final-version expectation to 11.
- **Import cycles** — `enchantments.ts`/`anvil.ts` may import `items.ts`; must not import
  `inventory.ts`. `xp.ts → enchantments.ts` is one-directional and safe.
- **Mending back-compat** — `mendXp` is a no-op (same ref, full `xpLeft`) without Mending
  gear, preserving all existing XP behavior/tests.

## Critical files

- `lib/game/engine/GameEngine.ts` — command handlers, `serialize()`
- `lib/game/enchantments.ts` — Mending def + `mendXp` seam
- `lib/game/engine/systems/xp.ts` — Mending wiring; `interact.ts` — station open
- `lib/game/save.ts` + `lib/game/types.ts` — v11, `customName`, `mending` id
- `lib/game/anvil.ts` / `grindstone.ts` (new) — pure logic
- `components/game/InventoryPanel.tsx` + `AnvilColumn.tsx`/`GrindstoneColumn.tsx` (new)
- `lib/world/blocks.ts` / `atlas.ts`, `lib/game/items.ts` / `recipes.ts` — new blocks

1	# Changelog
2	
3	All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.
4	
5	## [Unreleased]
6	
7	### Added
8	
9	- **Hardcore mode**: a per-world **permadeath** toggle on the new-world form, all on **zero new assets**. The save schema bumps **v9 → v10** (additive `hardcore` + `gameOver`), with **no worldgen change**
10	  - **Locked to Survival + Hard.** A hardcore world forces the game mode to Survival and the difficulty to Hard and **disables both pause-menu switchers** (immutable for the world's life), so there's no flipping to Creative or lowering the difficulty to cheat death. Its hearts render in a darker **withered** variant (a recolour of the procedural heart sprite)
11	  - **Death is permanent → spectate the dead world.** On death there is no respawn: the player flips to a **Spectator** free camera over their dead world (mobs keep roaming but can't touch them) and a **Game Over** screen offers _Spectate World_ (minimizes so you can fly around), _Back to Worlds_, or _Delete World_. The `gameOver` flag persists, so reloading a dead world resumes spectating — it can never be played again
12	  - **Architecture**: `hardcore` is a per-world boolean (`WorldMeta` + a v10 `SaveData` field + `migrateSaveV9toV10`), resolved first in the engine so it overrides mode/difficulty. The two lethal damage seams divert to a new `GameEngine.triggerGameOver()` (sets `gameOver`, switches to spectator, leaves `isDead` cleared so the respawn screen never shows); `switchGameMode`/`switchDifficulty` no-op under hardcore (the death transition sets the mode directly); the shell force-saves on the `gameOver` event. New `GameOverScreen` component + a `GameShell` delete-world path
13	- **Difficulty**: the game gains Minecraft's difficulty axis — **Peaceful**, **Easy**, **Normal**, and **Hard** — orthogonal to the game mode, picked at world creation and switchable any time from the pause menu, all on **zero new assets**. The save schema bumps **v8 → v9** (additive), with **no worldgen change**
14	  - **Peaceful**: no hostile mobs spawn (and switching to Peaceful instantly despawns every hostile already around — a safe panic button, the boss included), health regenerates **twice as fast**, and an empty hunger bar never hurts you — full survival minus the danger, distinct from Creative
15	  - **Easy / Normal / Hard** scale two things together: **mob hit damage** (×0.5 / ×1 / ×1.5, applied at the strike — the per-mob templates are never mutated) and **hostile spawning** (cadence + the concurrent cap, ×16 → 8 / 16 / 24)
16	  - **Starvation** (new): an empty hunger bar now has a consequence — half a heart every few seconds, down to a difficulty-scaled floor. Easy stops at 5 hearts, Normal at half a heart, and **Hard can starve you to death**; Peaceful never starves. (This changes existing **Normal** worlds: previously a fully-empty hunger bar did nothing.)
17	  - **Architecture**: a new `lib/game/difficulties.ts` holds the `Difficulty` union plus **accessor functions** (`hostilesSpawn`, `mobDamageMultiplier`, `hostileSpawnIntervalScale`, `hostileCapScale`, `regenIntervalScale`, `starves`/`starvationFloorHp`) that each system reads, mirroring the game-mode predicate pattern. Difficulty rides the same per-world plumbing as `gameMode` (`WorldMeta` + a v9 `SaveData` field + `migrateSaveV8toV9`); the spawn gate keys **only** on difficulty and the damage/threat gate **only** on game mode, so the two axes stay independent (Peaceful stops spawns even in Creative; Creative is invulnerable even on Hard). New `setDifficulty` command (`GameEngine.switchDifficulty`); new `STARVATION_INTERVAL_SECONDS`/`STARVATION_HP` tunables
18	- **Game modes**: the game gains Minecraft's four ways to play — **Survival** (the original), **Creative**, **Adventure**, and **Spectator** — as a single per-player axis you pick at world creation and can switch any time from the pause menu, all on **zero new assets**. The save schema bumps **v7 → v8** (additive), with **no worldgen change**
19	  - **Creative**: fly (double-tap **Space**, then Space/crouch to rise/descend), take no damage and never hunger, break any block instantly, and place blocks without consuming them. The recipe book is replaced by a searchable **palette of every item** — click one to pull a stack into your inventory. The survival HUD bars hide
20	  - **Adventure**: survival in every respect (damage, hunger, mobs, combat, doors/chests/trading) **except you can't break or place blocks**, so a built world stays intact
21	  - **Spectator**: a free camera — fly through terrain (noclip), invisible and invulnerable, with no interaction at all; hostiles ignore you entirely and the HUD/hotbar hide
22	  - **Switching** modes mid-game (pause menu) refills your bars and clears any pending hazard damage, sets flight to match the mode, and lifts you out of a wall when leaving Spectator — so it's always safe to flip between them
23	  - **Architecture**: a new `lib/game/gameModes.ts` holds the `GameMode` union plus **intent predicates** (`takesDamage`, `canEditBlocks`, `freeBuild`, `canInteract`, `canFly`, `isNoclip`, `usesInventory`, `mobsThreaten`) that each system gates on, rather than comparing the raw id — so the four modes share one set of seams (the damage chokepoints in `playerLife.ts`, the block edits in `mining.ts`, aggro in `mobAI.ts`, flight/noclip in `playerMotion.ts`). `gameMode` rides the existing per-world `worldType` plumbing (`WorldMeta` + a v8 `SaveData` field + `migrateSaveV7toV8`); unlike `worldType` it's the _current_, switchable value, and the transient `isFlying` is never serialized. 24	
25	### Changed
26	
27	- **Pause menu reorganized into tabs**: the Esc menu had grown into one long scrolling column (action buttons, the game-mode grid, volume sliders, the skin picker, and a 12-row controls list). It's now split into **Game** (save / load / reset / quit + game mode), **Options** (sound + appearance), and **Controls** (the key reference), with **Back to Game** pinned on top. Pure presentation — no save-format, worldgen, or behavior change (`components/game/PauseMenu.tsx`).
28	
29	## [0.10.0] - 2026-06-21
30	
31	### Added
32	
33	- **XP & enchanting**: the game gains its first progression currency and a way to spend it, all on **zero new assets** (a procedural XP bar + effect-coloured table sprite, synthesized blip/shimmer). The save schema bumps **v6 → v7** (additive), with **no worldgen change**
34	  - **XP** (`state.xp`, banked points; `XP_PER_LEVEL` points = one level): earned from **mob kills** (hostiles more than passives, the **boss a jackpot**; babies give none, like drops — table in `mobXp.ts`), **mining ores** (scaled by rarity), and **fishing** catches. 35	  - **Enchanting**: craft an **Enchanting Table** (2 diamond ore + 4 cobble) and right-click it to open the enchanting panel, then spend XP levels to enchant the **selected** tool/weapon/armor. 36	  - **Architecture**: enchantments are **per-item-instance data, like durability** (non-stackable gear, slot-cloned on insert), so the inventory algebra and persistence are reused — they ride the existing `SavedSlot` snapshot/restore (validated on load). XP/level math + the award/spend helpers live in `lib/game/engine/systems/xp.ts`; the readers + `canEnchant`/`applyEnchant` in `lib/game/enchantments.ts`. Enchanting is a new `enchant` command (not a recipe — `craft` produces a fixed result and can't mutate the held instance). The `EnchantingTable` `BlockId` is appended (id 52) so existing saved block ids never shift; `xp` and per-slot `enchantments` are additive v7 fields, so pre-XP saves load clean
37	- **Status effects, brewing & potions**: the game gains its first timed-buff system — six effects, five of them brewed into potions at a new station, all on **zero new assets** (procedural flask/icon sprites + a synthesized "glug"). The save schema bumps **v5 → v6** (additive), with **no worldgen change**
38	  - **Effects** (`state.effects`, a Map of id → remaining seconds): **Speed** (×1.2 movement), **Strength** (+3 melee damage), **Regeneration** (heals on its own cadence, even at low hunger), **Fire Resistance** (lava can't burn you), **Water Breathing** (lungs stay full, no drowning), and **Poison** (chips you down but **never kills** — floors at half a heart). Each is read at exactly one existing seam (movement speed, attack damage, the lava/oxygen ticks, or a per-tick accumulator), so the simulation stays modular. Re-applying an effect refreshes to the longer remaining time; all are cleared on death
39	  - **Brewing Stand** (craft 3 cobble + 1 gold ore): a new interactive block — right-click to open its **Brewing** recipes, exactly like a furnace opens smelting, reusing the whole `station`-recipe pipeline. Glass bottles come first (3 glass → 3 bottles), then a bottle + one reagent brews a potion: **feather → Swiftness**, **gunpowder → Strength**, **wheat → Regeneration**, **coal → Fire Resistance**, **raw fish → Water Breathing** (all existing drops/crops, so no new worldgen). Drink with the **F** key (the eat key is potion-aware); drinking consumes the whole bottle
40	  - **Poison hazard**: eating **rotten flesh** has an 80% chance to poison you — a real downside to the most desperate food. Poison is the only effect with no potion
41	  - **HUD**: active effects show as a stacked top-left column of procedural icon + m:ss countdown, opposite the minimap, hidden when nothing is active. The projection is cached and rebuilt only when the rounded seconds change, so it re-renders ~1 Hz instead of every frame
42	  - **Architecture**: effects live in a new `lib/game/engine/systems/statusEffects.ts` (helpers + `tickStatusEffects`, which runs after `tickHealthRegen` and before the environmental ticks so the fire-resist/water-breathing gates are current). Poison uses a **new** `applyNonLethalDamage` rather than the killing `applyUnmitigatedDamage`. The `BrewingStand` `BlockId` is appended at the end of the enum (id 51) so existing saved block ids never shift. Effects are additive on save v6 (a pure version bump; pre-effect saves load with none) and **cleared on death**, so a saved-then-reloaded world resumes whatever was active
43	- **Dragon Lord tracker**: while the boss lives, its top-center health HUD now includes a rotating pointer toward it and its horizontal distance in blocks, making it possible to reacquire the fight after terrain or summoned mobs break line of sight. The values are rounded before entering the React snapshot to avoid sub-block render churn. This is transient UI state with **no save-format or worldgen impact**.
44	- **Fishing**: water was only ever a hazard to avoid — now it's a place to fish, a relaxed renewable food source with the odd lucky find, all on **zero new assets** (a procedural rod/fish sprite + synthesized splashes). **No save-format or worldgen change** — the cast is transient session state and the new items save by string id
45	  - **Fishing rod** (craft 3 wood + 2 string): right-click while aiming at water to **cast** a bobber. After a random wait it **dips with a splash** (a bite) — right-click again within ~1.2 s to **reel in** a catch; miss the window and it gets away while the bobber keeps fishing

  - **Architecture**: effects live in a new `lib/game/engine/systems/statusEffects.ts` (helpers + `tickStatusEffects`, which runs after `tickHealthRegen` and before the environmental ticks so the fire-resist/water-breathing gates are current). Poison uses a **new** `applyNonLethalDamage` rather than the killing `applyUnmitigatedDamage`. The `BrewingStand` `BlockId` is appended at the end of the enum (id 51) so existing saved block ids never shift. Effects are additive on save v6 (a pure version bump; pre-effect saves load with none) and **cleared on death**, so a saved-then-reloaded world resumes whatever was active
- **Dragon Lord tracker**: while the boss lives, its top-center health HUD now includes a rotating pointer toward it and its horizontal distance in blocks, making it possible to reacquire the fight after terrain or summoned mobs break line of sight. The values are rounded before entering the React snapshot to avoid sub-block render churn. This is transient UI state with **no save-format or worldgen impact**.
- **Fishing**: water was only ever a hazard to avoid — now it's a place to fish, a relaxed renewable food source with the odd lucky find, all on **zero new assets** (a procedural rod/fish sprite + synthesized splashes). **No save-format or worldgen change** — the cast is transient session state and the new items save by string id
  - **Fishing rod** (craft 3 wood + 2 string): right-click while aiming at water to **cast** a bobber. After a random wait it **dips with a splash** (a bite) — right-click again within ~1.2 s to **reel in** a catch; miss the window and it gets away while the bobber keeps fishing

1	# Gameplay Reference
2	
3	Scannable tables for everything in the game: recipes, blocks, mobs, and item
4	stats. For how it all fits together, read the [player manual](manual.md).
5	
6	> **The code is the source of truth.** These tables are a convenience snapshot of
7	> `lib/game/recipes.ts`, `lib/game/items.ts`, `lib/world/blocks.ts`,
8	> `lib/game/mobs.ts`, and `lib/game/mobLoot.ts`. If a number here disagrees with
9	> the game, the code wins — and this page needs an update.
10	
11	## Game modes
12	
13	Chosen at world creation and switchable any time from the pause menu; saved with
14	the world and independent of the world type. Source: `lib/game/gameModes.ts` (the
15	`GameMode` union + predicates each system gates on).
16	
17	| Mode      | Damage / hunger | Break / place blocks   | Flight       | Interact (combat, doors, eat) | Mobs       | Inventory         |
18	| --------- | --------------- | ---------------------- | ------------ | ----------------------------- | ---------- | ----------------- |
19	| Survival  | Yes             | Yes                    | No           | Yes                           | Hostile    | Normal            |
20	| Creative  | No (invincible) | Instant, free (no use) | Yes          | Yes                           | Ignore you | All-items palette |
21	| Adventure | Yes             | **No**                 | No           | Yes                           | Hostile    | Normal            |
22	| Spectator | No (invincible) | No                     | Yes (noclip) | **No**                        | Ignore you | Hidden            |
23	
24	## Difficulty
25	
26	A separate axis from the game mode — also chosen at world creation, switchable from
27	the pause menu, and saved with the world. Sets how hard survival is. Source:
28	`lib/game/difficulties.ts` (the `Difficulty` union + accessors each system reads).
29	
30	| Level    | Hostiles spawn             | Mob damage | Spawn rate / cap  | Starvation            |
31	| -------- | -------------------------- | ---------- | ----------------- | --------------------- |
32	| Peaceful | No (and despawns existing) | —          | none / 0          | Never (regen ×2 fast) |
33	| Easy     | Yes                        | ×0.5       | slower / cap 8    | Stops at 5 hearts     |
34	| Normal   | Yes                        | ×1.0       | baseline / cap 16 | Stops at ½ heart      |
35	| Hard     | Yes                        | ×1.5       | faster / cap 24   | Kills you             |
36	
37	## Hardcore
38	
39	A per-world toggle (immutable, chosen at creation) for permadeath. Forces **Survival**
40	mode and **Hard** difficulty and locks both switchers. On death the run ends: the
41	world flips to a spectator "dead world" with a Game Over screen (Spectate / Back to
42	Worlds / Delete World), and the dead state persists across reloads. Hearts render in
43	a withered dark-red variant. Source: the `hardcore`/`gameOver` flags in
44	`lib/game/types.ts` + `GameEngine.triggerGameOver`.
45	
46	## World types
47	
48	Chosen when you create a world (alongside the name and seed) and fixed for its
49	life. All four share the same five biomes — they reshape terrain, not the biome
50	mix. Source: `lib/world/worldTypes.ts` + `terrainConfigFor` in `lib/world/generation.ts`.

53	| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
54	| Default   | Balanced terrain with every biome — the original generator                                  |
55	| Superflat | Level ground at a fixed height; a builder's canvas (caves and ores still generate below)    |
56	| Amplified | Exaggerated relief — towering peaks and deep valleys                                        |
57	| Islands   | A raised sea breaks the land into scattered, gently sloped islands with deep ocean channels |
58	
59	## Recipes
60	
61	**66 crafting recipes** (plus **10 villager trades**, listed under [Trading](#trading)).

git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
feat(enchanting): add Mending enchantment

The enchanting table had four enchantments that all made gear stronger, but
nothing kept gear alive — durability was a one-way countdown until a tool broke
and you re-crafted it. Mending closes that loop by turning XP, the game's
long-term currency, into a way to maintain your best gear.

Mending is a fifth enchantment applied at the existing table (like Unbreaking,
it takes any durable tool/weapon/armor). It's binary (max level 1). While it's
on the item you're holding or wearing, XP you pick up is diverted to repair that
item — MENDING_REPAIR_PER_XP (2) durability per point, held item first, then
equipped armor — and only the remainder is banked.

Implemented as one seam, `mendXp` in enchantments.ts, read once in `awardXp`, in
keeping with the one-reader-per-seam discipline. The event still reports the
gross amount so the HUD and sound react to the full pickup. The `mending` id
rides the existing per-slot `enchantments`, so no save-format bump is needed; it
is added to the save validator's known-id set so it survives restore.

The fishing test's minimal GameState mock gains `equippedArmor`, which `awardXp`
now reads through the Mending seam.
EOF

content.text: Save tests pass. Now the save-format doc:

content.content:
3:## Schema
5:`SaveData` (version 10) in `lib/game/types.ts`:
14:- inventory slots with durability **and enchantments** (36 slots; the first 9 are the hotbar). Each `SavedSlot` is `{ id, count, durability?, enchantments? }`; `enchantments` (`{ id, level }[]`) ride durable gear only and are validated on load (`restoreSlot` — known ids via `Object.hasOwn`, levels clamped to `1..ENCHANT_MAX_LEVEL`). The same path serializes chest contents
15:- `xp` (optional) — banked experience points (`XP_PER_LEVEL` points = one level). Earned from kills/ore/fishing, spent at the enchanting table. Restored by `restoreXp` (finite, ≥ 0). Unlike effects, XP is a currency and is **kept across death**
27:Audio volume preferences live under a **separate**, global key (`minecraft_audio_v1`, `lib/game/audio/settings.ts`), shared across all profiles and not part of any world save or its versioning.
37:### Version history
39:- **v10** (Hardcore) — adds optional top-level `hardcore` and `gameOver` booleans. `migrateSaveV9toV10` is a pure version bump (both absent ⇒ a normal, non-hardcore world, via `restoreHardcore`/`restoreGameOver`). `hardcore` is immutable (forces Survival + Hard, locks both switchers); `gameOver` is the persisted permadeath flag, so a dead hardcore world reloads into its spectator state rather than respawning (the transient `isDead`/`respawnTimer` remain session-only). No worldgen change — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
40:- **v9** (difficulty) — adds an optional top-level `difficulty` (`"peaceful"` | `"easy"` | `"normal"` | `"hard"`). `migrateSaveV8toV9` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ `"normal"`, via `restoreDifficulty`). Difficulty is an axis orthogonal to `gameMode`, switchable in-game, so the _current_ level is what's stored; the per-level multipliers live in `lib/game/difficulties.ts` and the `starvationTimer` accumulator is session-only. No worldgen change — difficulty touches no generation — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
41:- **v8** (game modes) — adds an optional top-level `gameMode` (`"survival"` | `"creative"` | `"adventure"` | `"spectator"`). `migrateSaveV7toV8` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ `"survival"`, via `restoreGameMode`). The mode is switchable in-game, so the _current_ mode is what's stored; the transient `isFlying` is never serialized. No worldgen change — modes touch no generation — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
42:- **v7** (XP & enchanting) — adds optional top-level `xp` and an optional `enchantments` array on each `SavedSlot`. `migrateSaveV6toV7` is a pure version bump (absent → xp 0, no enchantments). XP persists and is **kept across death** (it's a currency, not a status effect); enchantments ride the existing `inventorySlotsSnapshot`/`restoreSlot` path (shared by inventory and chests) and are validated on load. The **Enchanting Table** item saves by string id and the `EnchantingTable` `BlockId` is **appended** (id 52) so saved block ids never shift. No worldgen change — **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
43:- **v6** (status effects, brewing & potions) — adds optional `effects` (`{ id, remaining }[]`). `migrateSaveV5toV6` is a pure version bump (absent → no active effects), so pre-effect saves load clean. The fishing rod and raw/cooked fish are additive items saved by string id, and a catch is an ordinary inventory change. No worldgen change, so neither the `version` nor `WORLDGEN_VERSION` moved.
45:- **v5** (unchanged for the living world — saplings, bone meal & grass spread) — every effect is an ordinary block edit that rides the `changes` diff: a planted sapling, a grown tree's wood and leaves, and re-grassed dirt all persist with no new fields, and bone meal is an additive item saved by string id. The `Sapling` `BlockId` is **appended at the end** of the enum (id 50) so existing saved block ids never shift. Crucially, the runtime tree grower (`systems/treeGrowth.ts`) shares **no** code with worldgen's hash-pinned `placeTrees`, so the generated terrain is byte-identical and **neither the `version` nor `WORLDGEN_VERSION` moved**.
46:- **v5** (unchanged for villagers & trading) — the villager mob is transient like every mob, and trading needs no persisted state: a trade is a station-gated recipe (`station: "villager"`) run through the existing `craft` command, the open trade station (`craftingStation`) is session-only, and there are no per-trade use caps to store. **Emerald** and any traded goods save by string id in the existing inventory slots. 47:- **v5** (unchanged for creepers & TNT) — the creeper mob, gunpowder, and the explosion system add no persisted state: mobs are transient, **a creeper's lit fuse and a primed TNT block's countdown are session-only** (`MobState.fuseTimer` and `state.primedTnt` are never serialized — like the boss and in-flight arrows). Gunpowder and the TNT item save by string id; a **placed TNT block persists in the block diff** like any block, and a save written mid-fuse reloads with that TNT as an inert, un-lit block (and no creeper). There is no worldgen change — creepers are spawned and TNT is crafted — so neither the `version` nor `WORLDGEN_VERSION` moved. Blast-destroyed blocks are ordinary block-diff edits.
48:- **v5** (unchanged for cow/pig & coal) — the cow and pig mobs (and their meat/leather drops) add no persisted state; mobs are transient and the new foods save by string id. Coal ore, coal, and charcoal are likewise additive (the ore persists in the block diff, the items by string id), so the save _schema_ stays at version 5. But the new coal worldgen changes the deterministic terrain baseline, so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` is bumped `7` → `8`**: a world whose recorded version differs discards its stale block-diffs and reboots from its seed. 49:- **v5** (unchanged for caves & lighting) — the lighting system adds no persisted state (light is a derived cache, recomputed at load), and lava is worldgen, not a saved field. So the save _schema_ stays at version 5. But the deep-cave lava changes the deterministic terrain baseline, so **`SAVE_KEY` is bumped `minecraft_save_v6` → `minecraft_save_v7`**: old block-diffs were computed against the lava-free world and must never be applied to the new one. Pre-lava saves are discarded in practice. Torches are additive items/blocks, persisted by string id / in the block diff like any other placed block.

52:- **v4** — adds optional `blockEntities` (chest contents). `migrateSaveV3toV4` is a pure version bump (absent → restores as no containers), so **`SAVE_KEY` was unchanged** at the time (player-placed chests only; worldgen and the index formula were untouched) and v1/v2/v3 saves load fine.
53:- **v3** — adds optional `dayClock`, `hearts`, `hunger`, and `spawnPoint`. `migrateSaveV2toV3` is a pure version bump (the new fields stay absent and restore as engine defaults), so **`SAVE_KEY` is unchanged** and v1/v2 saves load fine.
56:- Unknown future versions are rejected (treated as no save).
58:## Profiles & worlds
60:Saves are organized two levels deep — a **profile** owns a list of **worlds**, and each world holds one `SaveData` blob — across three localStorage keys. All three are versioned `{ version: 1, ... }` envelopes and their readers are **total** (malformed entries are dropped, never thrown):
66:`worldgenVersion` records the `WORLDGEN_VERSION` (`lib/game/config.ts`, currently 8) the world was generated under. This **replaces the old whole-store `SAVE_KEY` bump**: when the worldgen baseline changes, bump `WORLDGEN_VERSION`, and a world whose recorded version differs has its stale block-diffs discarded and reboots from its stored seed — per-world, with no key rename and without touching unaffected worlds.

# Save format & compatibility

## Schema

`SaveData` (version 10) in `lib/game/types.ts`:

- world `seed`
- `worldType` (optional) — the generation preset (`"default"` | `"flat"` | `"amplified"` | `"islands"`); absent ⇒ `"default"`. Like `seed`, it is fixed for the world's life and the world must always regenerate with it, since the block-diffs were recorded against that terrain
- `gameMode` (optional) — the player's game mode (`"survival"` | `"creative"` | `"adventure"` | `"spectator"`); absent ⇒ `"survival"`. Unlike `worldType`, this is **switchable in-game** (pause menu), so the saved value is the _current_ mode, not the one chosen at creation. Restored by `restoreGameMode` (`lib/game/save.ts`); `isFlying` is session-only and never serialized
- `difficulty` (optional) — the player's difficulty (`"peaceful"` | `"easy"` | `"normal"` | `"hard"`); absent ⇒ `"normal"`. An axis orthogonal to `gameMode`, and likewise **switchable in-game** (pause menu), so the saved value is the _current_ difficulty. Restored by `restoreDifficulty` (`lib/game/save.ts`); the per-level multipliers live in `lib/game/difficulties.ts`, the starvation accumulator (`starvationTimer`) is session-only
- `hardcore` (optional) — the Hardcore flag (`boolean`); absent ⇒ `false`. **Immutable** (unlike `gameMode`/`difficulty`): a hardcore world is forced to Survival + Hard and the engine locks both switchers. Restored by `restoreHardcore`
- `gameOver` (optional) — the permadeath flag (`boolean`); absent ⇒ `false`. Set once a hardcore run has ended in death; a reloaded `gameOver` world boots into the spectator "dead world" state (never playable). Restored by `restoreGameOver`. (The transient `isDead`/`respawnTimer` stay session-only — hardcore death is captured by this flag instead.)
- a block **diff** list — `changes: [blockIndex, blockId][]`; edits that revert to the generated baseline are pruned (player-placed crops, beds, furnaces, chests, and both halves/states of doors ride this list — they are ordinary block edits)
- inventory slots with durability **and enchantments** (36 slots; the first 9 are the hotbar). Each `SavedSlot` is `{ id, count, durability?, enchantments? }`; `enchantments` (`{ id, level }[]`) ride durable gear only and are validated on load (`restoreSlot` — known ids via `Object.hasOwn`, levels clamped to `1..ENCHANT_MAX_LEVEL`). The same path serializes chest contents
- `xp` (optional) — banked experience points (`XP_PER_LEVEL` points = one level). Earned from kills/ore/fishing, spent at the enchanting table. Restored by `restoreXp` (finite, ≥ 0). Unlike effects, XP is a currency and is **kept across death**
- equipped armor
- selected hotbar slot (0–8)
- player position — validated on load by `restorePlayerPosition` (`lib/game/save.ts`): coords keep their fractional part (the player isn't grid-aligned) but a missing or non-finite (NaN/Infinity) position is rejected, leaving the fresh spawn in place so a corrupt blob can't load a broken world or slip past the `position.y < 2` unstuck net
- `dayClock`, `hearts`, `hunger` (all optional) — time of day and player stats, so sleeping through the night and a hurt/hungry player survive a reload
- `spawnPoint` (optional, `{x,y,z}` or null) — the bed respawn point; respawn falls back to a random land point when it is null or the block there is no longer a bed

lines: - **v5** (unchanged for cow/pig & coal) — the cow and pig mobs (and their meat/leather drops) add no persisted state; mobs are transient and the new foods save by string id. Coal ore, coal, and charcoal are likewise additive (the ore persists in the block diff, the items by string id), so the save _schema_ stays at version 5. But the new coal worldgen changes the deterministic terrain baseline, so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` is bumped `7` → `8`**: a world whose recorded version differs discards its stale block-diffs and reboots from its seed. Coal runs on its own PRNG (`placeCoal`), so only underground coal cells differ from a v7 world — the surface, existing ores, trees, and structures are byte-identical (the meshing and structural-probe tests stay green; only the byte hashes were re-rolled).

- **v5** (unchanged for caves & lighting) — the lighting system adds no persisted state (light is a derived cache, recomputed at load), and lava is worldgen, not a saved field. So the save _schema_ stays at version 5. But the deep-cave lava changes the deterministic terrain baseline, so **`SAVE_KEY` is bumped `minecraft_save_v6` → `minecraft_save_v7`**: old block-diffs were computed against the lava-free world and must never be applied to the new one. Pre-lava saves are discarded in practice. Torches are additive items/blocks, persisted by string id / in the block diff like any other placed block.

- **v5** (unchanged for ranged combat & the endgame boss) — bows, arrows, the Cursed Totem, the Dragon Heart, and the Dragon Sword are **additive items**, persisted by string id in the existing inventory/container slots, so no schema change was needed. **Arrows in flight, the boss, its minions, and the `victory` flag are all transient** (never serialized — like mobs), and there is no worldgen change (the boss is summoned, not generated), so neither the `version` nor `SAVE_KEY` moved.

-- **v5** — adds optional `lootedChests` (opened/broken dungeon loot chests). `migrateSaveV4toV5` is a pure version bump (absent → no dungeon chests yet looted). Unlike v3/v4, **`SAVE_KEY` is bumped to `minecraft_save_v6`** here — not because of the save _shape_ (the field is additive) but because the dungeon worldgen changed the deterministic terrain baseline, so old block-diffs would index against the wrong world. Pre-dungeon saves are therefore discarded in practice; the migration keeps the version chain complete regardless. `readSave` chains v1 → v2 → v3 → v4 → v5 → v6 → v7 → v8 → v9 → v10.

- **v4** — adds optional `blockEntities` (chest contents). `migrateSaveV3toV4` is a pure version bump (absent → restores as no containers), so **`SAVE_KEY` was unchanged** at the time (player-placed chests only; worldgen and the index formula were untouched) and v1/v2/v3 saves load fine.

- **v3** — adds optional `dayClock`, `hearts`, `hunger`, and `spawnPoint`. `migrateSaveV2toV3` is a pure version bump (the new fields stay absent and restore as engine defaults), so **`SAVE_KEY` is unchanged** and v1/v2 saves load fine.

git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
feat(save): bump save format to v11 with per-item custom names

The upcoming anvil lets a player rename gear, which needs somewhere to persist
that name. This adds the storage layer ahead of the feature so the format change
lands as its own reviewable, bisectable unit.

`SavedSlot`/`InventorySlot` gain an optional `customName`; `SaveData` becomes v11
with a pure `migrateSaveV10toV11` bump, chained into `readSave`. The name is
snapshotted with the other per-slot fields and restored only on durable gear
(the same population as enchantments and the rename feature), trimmed and capped
to the new `CUSTOM_NAME_MAX_LEN` with blanks dropped, so a hand-edited blob can't
inject an unbounded or whitespace name. Nothing writes `customName` yet — the
anvil does that in a later commit — so this is additive and pre-v11 saves load
unchanged.

No worldgen change (WORLDGEN_VERSION stays 8). Updates the save round-trip tests
(final version 11, new custom-name cases) and the two engine tests that assert
the serialized version.
EOF

export type MaterialGroup = "stone" | "wood" | "grass" | "sand" | "glass" | "water";

over it. You gain XP for **killing mobs** (tougher mobs give more — the boss is a
big payout), **mining ores** (rarer ores give more), and **reeling in fish**. XP
is a currency, so unlike potion effects it **stays with you when you die**.

Spend it at an **enchanting table** (craft one from **2 diamond ore + 4 cobble**).
Place it, right-click to open the enchanting panel, then **select** the tool,
weapon, or armor you want to improve in your hotbar — the panel shows the
enchantments it can take. Each costs **3 levels** and can be applied up to **three
times**:

- **Sharpness** (weapons) — hit harder in melee
- **Protection** (armor) — take less damage
- **Efficiency** (tools) — mine faster
- **Unbreaking** (any gear) — gear lasts longer (it sometimes ignores wear)
- **Mending** (any gear) — XP you pick up repairs the held or worn item instead of
  banking, as long as it's damaged

Buttons grey out when you can't afford the cost or the enchant is maxed.
Enchantments are part of the item, so they're kept in chests and across reloads.
Full numbers are in the [reference](reference.md#xp--enchanting).

## The anvil

Craft an **anvil** (**3 gold ore + 4 cobble**), place it, and right-click to open
the anvil panel. Like the enchanting table it works on the **selected** hotbar
item — a tool, weapon, or armor piece — and spends XP levels:

- **Combine** a second copy of the same item into it. The result keeps the best of
  both: its durability is restored (the two bars added together, plus a bonus) and
  any enchantments are merged, taking the higher level of each. The duplicate is
  used up. Costs **4 levels**.
- **Repair** with raw material — feed it the item's tier material (e.g. a diamond
  sword takes **diamond ore**, a stone pickaxe takes **cobble**) to restore a chunk
  of durability without needing a second copy. Costs **1 level** per material unit.
- **Rename** the item to anything you like (it shows everywhere the item's name
  does). Costs **1 level**.

Buttons grey out when there's nothing to do (no duplicate, full durability, or no
matching material) or you can't afford the cost. For passive, no-table upkeep,
enchant gear with **Mending** instead.

## The anvil

Craft an **anvil** (**3 gold ore + 4 cobble**), place it, and right-click to open
the anvil panel. Like the enchanting table it works on the **selected** hotbar
item — a tool, weapon, or armor piece — and spends XP levels:

- **Combine** a second copy of the same item into it. The result keeps the best of
  both: its durability is restored (the two bars added together, plus a bonus) and
  any enchantments are merged, taking the higher level of each. The duplicate is
  used up. Costs **4 levels**.
- **Repair** with raw material — feed it the item's tier material (e.g. a diamond
  sword takes **diamond ore**, a stone pickaxe takes **cobble**) to restore a chunk
  of durability without needing a second copy. Costs **1 level** per material unit.
- **Rename** the item to anything you like (it shows everywhere the item's name
  does). Costs **1 level**.

Buttons grey out when there's nothing to do (no duplicate, full durability, or no
matching material) or you can't afford the cost. For passive, no-table upkeep,
enchant gear with **Mending** instead.

5:## A new block
7:1. Add to the `BlockId` enum and `BLOCK_COLORS` in `lib/world/blocks.ts` — the atlas auto-generates its tile. Add a `HELD_BLOCK_COLORS` entry for the first-person model tint.
9:3. Make it placeable/droppable: an `ITEM_DEFS` entry (`kind: "block"`, `blockId`) plus a `BLOCK_TO_SLOT` mapping — without the mapping, mining it drops nothing. The inventory icon (isometric cube) auto-generates from `BLOCK_COLORS`; ore-style blocks can add an accent color in `lib/ui/spritePixels.ts` (`ORE_ACCENTS`).
12:6. Map it to a sound family in `lib/game/audio/materials.ts` — the `BlockId → MaterialGroup` record is exhaustive, so typecheck fails until the entry exists.
16:## A new item or recipe
30:- Recipes are `{ id, label, cost: [{slotId, count}], result: {slotId, count} }` in `lib/game/recipes.ts`. An optional `station` makes a recipe station-gated: it only crafts while that station's panel is open, enforced in the `craft` command and shown locked in the recipe book. The stations are `"furnace"` (smelting), `"villager"` (a **trade** — see below), and `"brewing"` (potions, opened at a brewing stand). Adding a station means extending that union in **four** places (`Recipe.station` in `types.ts`, `craftingStation` on both `GameState` and `GameSnapshot` in `state.ts`, and the `openedStation` event), plus a `RecipeCategory` + a `recipeCategory()` branch and a `STATION_LABELS` entry (`InventoryPanel.tsx`).
31:- **Villager trades** (`lib/game/trades.ts`) ARE just `station: "villager"` recipes spread into `RECIPES`, so they reuse the whole crafting pipeline and recipe-book UI for free. To open them, an interaction sets `state.craftingStation = "villager"` (right-clicking a villager via `tryTradeAimedVillager` in `interact.ts`); the panel then shows the trades as a **Trading** book and the `craft` command runs them. Emerald is the currency — add sell offers (material → emerald) and buy offers (emerald → goods) to keep the economy two-sided. There's no persisted trade state, so this needs no save-format change.

76:## An interactive block (right-click behavior)
78:- Right-click (and KeyE) dispatch `placeBlock`, which runs a fixed precedence in `GameEngine.dispatch` before falling through to placement: feed an aimed mob → `tryInteractBlock` → use the held item → place. To make a block do something on right-click, register it in `INTERACTIVE_BLOCKS` and add a branch in `tryInteractBlock` (`lib/game/engine/systems/interact.ts`).
80:- Four reference implementations: the **door** atomically toggles matching upper/lower state IDs; the **bed** sets `state.spawnPoint` and starts the sleep fade (`state.sleepTimer`); the **furnace** opens the inventory and sets `state.craftingStation`, which unlocks its `station` recipes (see "A new item or recipe"); the **chest** opens the inventory and sets `state.openContainerIndex` (see below). A block that opens the inventory from a mouse click also needs an `openedStation`/`openedContainer` handler in `useMinecraftGame` to release pointer lock. See [architecture.md](architecture.md) for the step order.
82:## A container block (block-entity storage)
84:- Blocks are bare `BlockId`s, so any block that needs **attached data** (a chest's items) stores it in `state.containers: Map<voxelIndex, InventorySlot[]>`, keyed by `world.index(x,y,z)`. The chest is the reference:
85:  - **Open**: `interactChest` (an `INTERACTIVE_BLOCKS` branch) lazily creates the slot array, sets `state.openContainerIndex`, opens the inventory, and emits `openedContainer`. The snapshot exposes `container`, and `InventoryPanel` renders a second grid; `toggleInventory`/`pause` clear `openContainerIndex`.
90:## A random-tick behavior (growth / spread)
92:- Block updates that happen "over time" run through `lib/game/engine/systems/randomTicks.ts`: every `RANDOM_TICK_INTERVAL_SECONDS` it samples `RANDOM_TICK_SAMPLES` columns within `RANDOM_TICK_RADIUS` of the player and runs a handler on each column's top block. Register a `BlockId → handler` in `RANDOM_TICK_HANDLERS`; the handler edits via `state.blockChanges` and sets `state.worldMeshDirty`.
95:- A growing block also needs the usual block plumbing — a `BlockId` (appended at the end of the enum so saved ids don't shift), `BLOCK_COLORS` + an atlas paint branch (plants reuse the wheat trick: a solid cube painted to read as a plant, so no new geometry), an exhaustive `GROUP_BY_BLOCK` sound entry, and `BREAK_HARDNESS`/`BLOCK_TO_SLOT`/`rollBlockDrops`. A new **material** item (e.g. bone meal) must also get an `ITEM_SPRITE_GRIDS` entry, or the sprite test fails its no-magenta-checker assertion.

110:## A loot table / lazy block-entity fill
115:## A status effect (timed buff / hazard)
