1	# Gameplay Reference
2	
3	Scannable tables for everything in the game: recipes, blocks, mobs, and item
4	stats. For how it all fits together, read the [player manual](manual.md).
5	
6	> **The code is the source of truth.** These tables are a convenience snapshot of
7	> `lib/game/recipes.ts`, `lib/game/items.ts`, `lib/world/blocks.ts`,
8	> `lib/game/mobs.ts`, and `lib/game/mobLoot.ts`. If a number here disagrees with
9	> the game, the code wins — and this page needs an update.
10	
11	## Game modes
12	
13	Chosen at world creation and switchable any time from the pause menu; saved with
14	the world and independent of the world type. Source: `lib/game/gameModes.ts` (the
15	`GameMode` union + predicates each system gates on).
16	
17	| Mode      | Damage / hunger | Break / place blocks   | Flight       | Interact (combat, doors, eat) | Mobs       | Inventory         |
18	| --------- | --------------- | ---------------------- | ------------ | ----------------------------- | ---------- | ----------------- |
19	| Survival  | Yes             | Yes                    | No           | Yes                           | Hostile    | Normal            |
20	| Creative  | No (invincible) | Instant, free (no use) | Yes          | Yes                           | Ignore you | All-items palette |
21	| Adventure | Yes             | **No**                 | No           | Yes                           | Hostile    | Normal            |
22	| Spectator | No (invincible) | No                     | Yes (noclip) | **No**                        | Ignore you | Hidden            |
23	
24	## Difficulty
25	
26	A separate axis from the game mode — also chosen at world creation, switchable from
27	the pause menu, and saved with the world. Sets how hard survival is. Source:
28	`lib/game/difficulties.ts` (the `Difficulty` union + accessors each system reads).
29	
30	| Level    | Hostiles spawn             | Mob damage | Spawn rate / cap  | Starvation            |
31	| -------- | -------------------------- | ---------- | ----------------- | --------------------- |
32	| Peaceful | No (and despawns existing) | —          | none / 0          | Never (regen ×2 fast) |
33	| Easy     | Yes                        | ×0.5       | slower / cap 8    | Stops at 5 hearts     |
34	| Normal   | Yes                        | ×1.0       | baseline / cap 16 | Stops at ½ heart      |
35	| Hard     | Yes                        | ×1.5       | faster / cap 24   | Kills you             |
36	
37	## Hardcore
38	
39	A per-world toggle (immutable, chosen at creation) for permadeath. Forces **Survival**
40	mode and **Hard** difficulty and locks both switchers. On death the run ends: the
41	world flips to a spectator "dead world" with a Game Over screen (Spectate / Back to
42	Worlds / Delete World), and the dead state persists across reloads. Hearts render in
43	a withered dark-red variant. Source: the `hardcore`/`gameOver` flags in
44	`lib/game/types.ts` + `GameEngine.triggerGameOver`.
45	
46	## World types
47	
48	Chosen when you create a world (alongside the name and seed) and fixed for its
49	life. All four share the same five biomes — they reshape terrain, not the biome
50	mix. Source: `lib/world/worldTypes.ts` + `terrainConfigFor` in `lib/world/generation.ts`.

52	| Type      | Terrain                                                                                     |
53	| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
54	| Default   | Balanced terrain with every biome — the original generator                                  |
55	| Superflat | Level ground at a fixed height; a builder's canvas (caves and ores still generate below)    |
56	| Amplified | Exaggerated relief — towering peaks and deep valleys                                        |
57	| Islands   | A raised sea breaks the land into scattered, gently sloped islands with deep ocean channels |
58	
59	## Recipes
60	
61	**66 crafting recipes** (plus **10 villager trades**, listed under [Trading](#trading)).
62	All use the always-available crafting grid except the nine **furnace** smelting
63	recipes (need an open furnace) and the five **brewing** recipes (need an open

git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
feat(anvil): add Anvil for repairing, combining, and renaming gear

Enchanting could only make gear stronger; there was no way to keep a worn,
enchanted item alive or to consolidate two partial items. The anvil is the
gear-maintenance counterpart, completing the XP/enchanting progression loop.

Craft an anvil (3 gold ore + 4 cobble) and right-click it to open a panel that —
like the enchanting table — acts on the selected hotbar tool/weapon/armor and
spends XP levels:

- Combine a duplicate: add both durability bars plus a bonus and merge their
  enchantments at the higher level, consuming the duplicate.
- Repair with the item's tier material (diamond ore for a diamond sword, cobble
  for a stone pickaxe, …) for a chunk of durability without needing a second copy.
- Rename the item; the custom name shows everywhere its label does.

It follows the lean station idiom: no transient working slots (durable gear is
count:1, so combine/repair can't dupe or split a stack), pure logic in
lib/game/anvil.ts driven by anvilCombine/anvilRepair/anvilRename commands, and a
new AnvilColumn panel. The anvil station id is threaded through the engine/UI
craftingStation union only — not Recipe.station — so its actions aren't
recipe-gated. The Anvil BlockId is appended (id 53), craft-only, so no
WORLDGEN_VERSION bump. The rename rides the v11 customName field, surfaced
everywhere through a shared displayName helper.

Adds unit tests (anvil pure logic), engine tests (open/combine/repair/rename
happy paths + refusals + item-count conservation), and an AnvilColumn component
test; updates the manual, reference, adding-content, and CHANGELOG.
EOF

## XP & enchanting

`XP_PER_LEVEL`, `FISHING_XP`, `ENCHANT_MAX_LEVEL`, `ENCHANT_COST_LEVELS`,
`SHARPNESS_DAMAGE_PER_LEVEL`, `PROTECTION_DEFENSE_PER_LEVEL`,
`EFFICIENCY_SPEED_PER_LEVEL`, `UNBREAKING_SKIP_PER_LEVEL`, `MENDING_MAX_LEVEL`,
`MENDING_REPAIR_PER_XP`.

XP banks as points; `XP_PER_LEVEL` (10) points make one level. The per-mob and
per-ore XP tables live in `mobXp.ts` / `systems/xp.ts` (not here, like
`mobLoot.ts`); `FISHING_XP` (2) is the per-catch reward. Enchanting costs
`ENCHANT_COST_LEVELS` (3) levels per application, up to `ENCHANT_MAX_LEVEL` (3).
Each enchant is a flat per-level modifier read at one seam:
Sharpness `+SHARPNESS_DAMAGE_PER_LEVEL` (2) melee damage (`combat.ts` dispatch),
Protection `+PROTECTION_DEFENSE_PER_LEVEL` (2) defense (`equippedDefense` →
`armorReduction`), Efficiency `×(1 + EFFICIENCY_SPEED_PER_LEVEL × level)` mining
speed (`miningSpeed`), Unbreaking a `UNBREAKING_SKIP_PER_LEVEL` (0.2)
skip-chance per level (`consumeToolDurability`/`consumeEquippedArmorDurability`),
and Mending (`MENDING_MAX_LEVEL` 1, binary) diverting gained XP to repair
`MENDING_REPAIR_PER_XP` (2) durability per point on the held/worn item (`mendXp`,
read once in `awardXp`). Lower the costs or raise the magnitudes for faster
progression; the XP-source tables are the earning dial.

## Anvil & grindstone

`ANVIL_COMBINE_COST_LEVELS`, `ANVIL_REPAIR_COST_LEVELS`, `ANVIL_RENAME_COST_LEVELS`,
`ANVIL_REPAIR_BONUS_PCT`, `ANVIL_MATERIAL_REPAIR_PCT`, `CUSTOM_NAME_MAX_LEN`,
`GRINDSTONE_REFUND_XP_PER_LEVEL`.

The anvil spends XP levels to maintain gear (`lib/game/anvil.ts`, applied in
`GameEngine.dispatch`): **combine** a duplicate for `ANVIL_COMBINE_COST_LEVELS` (4) —
the two durabilities add together plus a `ANVIL_REPAIR_BONUS_PCT` (0.12 × max) bonus,
and enchantments merge at the higher level; **material repair** for
`ANVIL_REPAIR_COST_LEVELS` (1) restores `ANVIL_MATERIAL_REPAIR_PCT` (0.25 × max)
durability per material unit; **rename** for `ANVIL_RENAME_COST_LEVELS` (1) sets a
custom name capped at `CUSTOM_NAME_MAX_LEN` (32). The grindstone is the inverse — it
**strips** all enchantments and refunds `GRINDSTONE_REFUND_XP_PER_LEVEL` (5) XP points
per level removed (`lib/game/grindstone.ts`). Raise the repair percentages or lower
the costs to make upkeep cheaper; raise the grindstone refund to make disenchanting
more rewarding. The repair-material map (which material mends which gear) lives in
`REPAIR_MATERIAL_BY_ITEM` in `items.ts`.

1	# Gameplay Reference
2	
3	Scannable tables for everything in the game: recipes, blocks, mobs, and item
4	stats. For how it all fits together, read the [player manual](manual.md).
5	
6	> **The code is the source of truth.** These tables are a convenience snapshot of
7	> `lib/game/recipes.ts`, `lib/game/items.ts`, `lib/world/blocks.ts`,
8	> `lib/game/mobs.ts`, and `lib/game/mobLoot.ts`. If a number here disagrees with
9	> the game, the code wins — and this page needs an update.
10	
11	## Game modes
12	
13	Chosen at world creation and switchable any time from the pause menu; saved with
14	the world and independent of the world type. Source: `lib/game/gameModes.ts` (the
15	`GameMode` union + predicates each system gates on).
16	
17	| Mode      | Damage / hunger | Break / place blocks   | Flight       | Interact (combat, doors, eat) | Mobs       | Inventory         |
18	| --------- | --------------- | ---------------------- | ------------ | ----------------------------- | ---------- | ----------------- |
19	| Survival  | Yes             | Yes                    | No           | Yes                           | Hostile    | Normal            |
20	| Creative  | No (invincible) | Instant, free (no use) | Yes          | Yes                           | Ignore you | All-items palette |
21	| Adventure | Yes             | **No**                 | No           | Yes                           | Hostile    | Normal            |
22	| Spectator | No (invincible) | No                     | Yes (noclip) | **No**                        | Ignore you | Hidden            |
23	
24	## Difficulty
25	
26	A separate axis from the game mode — also chosen at world creation, switchable from
27	the pause menu, and saved with the world. Sets how hard survival is. Source:
28	`lib/game/difficulties.ts` (the `Difficulty` union + accessors each system reads).
29	
30	| Level    | Hostiles spawn             | Mob damage | Spawn rate / cap  | Starvation            |
31	| -------- | -------------------------- | ---------- | ----------------- | --------------------- |
32	| Peaceful | No (and despawns existing) | —          | none / 0          | Never (regen ×2 fast) |
33	| Easy     | Yes                        | ×0.5       | slower / cap 8    | Stops at 5 hearts     |
34	| Normal   | Yes                        | ×1.0       | baseline / cap 16 | Stops at ½ heart      |
35	| Hard     | Yes                        | ×1.5       | faster / cap 24   | Kills you             |
36	
37	## Hardcore
38	
39	A per-world toggle (immutable, chosen at creation) for permadeath. Forces **Survival**
40	mode and **Hard** difficulty and locks both switchers. On death the run ends: the
41	world flips to a spectator "dead world" with a Game Over screen (Spectate / Back to
42	Worlds / Delete World), and the dead state persists across reloads. Hearts render in
43	a withered dark-red variant. Source: the `hardcore`/`gameOver` flags in
44	`lib/game/types.ts` + `GameEngine.triggerGameOver`.
45	
46	## World types
47	
48	Chosen when you create a world (alongside the name and seed) and fixed for its
49	life. All four share the same five biomes — they reshape terrain, not the biome
50	mix. Source: `lib/world/worldTypes.ts` + `terrainConfigFor` in `lib/world/generation.ts`.
51	
52	| Type      | Terrain                                                                                     |
53	| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
54	| Default   | Balanced terrain with every biome — the original generator                                  |
55	| Superflat | Level ground at a fixed height; a builder's canvas (caves and ores still generate below)    |
56	| Amplified | Exaggerated relief — towering peaks and deep valleys                                        |
57	| Islands   | A raised sea breaks the land into scattered, gently sloped islands with deep ocean channels |
58	
59	## Recipes
60	
61	**66 crafting recipes** (plus **10 villager trades**, listed under [Trading](#trading)).
62	All use the always-available crafting grid except the nine **furnace** smelting
63	recipes (need an open furnace) and the five **brewing** recipes (need an open
64	[brewing stand](#brewing--potions)).
65	
66	In-game, the recipe book groups recipes into the sections below (Tools, Weapons,
67	Armor, Building, Food, Materials, then Smelting, Brewing, and Trades), listing the
68	recipes you can currently afford first within each section. Hovering a recipe you

git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
feat(grindstone): add Grindstone to strip enchantments for XP

The anvil consolidates and repairs gear, but there was no way to undo an
enchantment or salvage value from gear you've outgrown. The grindstone is the
inverse station: it removes enchantments and pays XP back.

Craft a grindstone (2 cobble + 2 planks) and right-click it to open a panel that —
like the anvil — acts on the selected hotbar gear. With an enchanted item
selected, "Remove enchantments" strips them all and refunds
GRINDSTONE_REFUND_XP_PER_LEVEL (5) XP per level removed. It costs nothing to use;
it only returns XP.

Same lean idiom as the anvil: pure logic in lib/game/grindstone.ts, a
grindstoneStrip command gated on the grindstone station, and a GrindstoneColumn
panel threaded through the engine/UI craftingStation union (not Recipe.station).
The Grindstone BlockId is appended (id 54), craft-only, so no WORLDGEN_VERSION
bump and no save-format change (it touches no persisted state).

Adds grindstone unit tests, an engine test (open/strip/refund + refusals), and a
GrindstoneColumn component test; updates the manual, reference, and CHANGELOG, and
backfills the anvil + grindstone tunables in tuning.md.
EOF
git log --oneline -4

Done. The **Anvil, Grindstone & Gear Progression** feature is fully implemented on branch `feat/anvil-grindstone-mending`, working tree clean.

## What landed (5 commits)

1. **`feat(enchanting): add Mending enchantment`** — a 5th enchantment at the existing table; gained XP repairs held/worn gear via a single `mendXp` seam in `awardXp`.
2. **`feat(save): bump save format to v11`** — per-item `customName`, pure v10→v11 migration, restored durable-only and sanitized.
3. **`feat(anvil): … repairing, combining, and renaming gear`** — new craft-only Anvil block; combine a duplicate (durability + merged enchants), material repair, and rename, all on the selected hotbar item for XP.
4. **`feat(grindstone): … strip enchantments for XP`** — new craft-only Grindstone block; removes all enchants and refunds XP.
5. **`test(e2e): expect save version 11`** — reconciled the reload smoke test with the v11 bump.

## Verification — all green
- `lint`, `typecheck`, `format:check`, `build` ✓
- `bun test` — **820 pass / 0 fail** (added: `anvil`, `grindstone`, `AnvilColumn`, `GrindstoneColumn` suites + engine, save, recipe, mending/xp cases)
- `bun run test:e2e` — **17 passed**

Each commit is bisectable (green on the unit gate), has a "why" body, and ships its own docs (`manual`, `reference`, `tuning`, `save-format`, `adding-content`) + `CHANGELOG`. No `Co-Authored-By` trailers, no `WORLDGEN_VERSION` bump (both blocks are craft-only).

A few defaults worth a glance in review (all easy `config.ts` tunables): recipe costs (Anvil = 3 gold ore + 4 cobble, Grindstone = 2 cobble + 2 planks), XP costs (combine 4 / repair 1 / rename 1), repair percentages, and the grindstone refund (5 XP/level).

Completes the XP/enchanting progression arc with gear maintenance and consolidation. Five focused commits, each green on the unit gate; full suite (820 unit + 17 e2e) and build are green.

## What's new

- **Mending enchantment** — a 5th enchantment at the existing enchanting table (any durable gear, binary). Gained XP is diverted to repair the held/worn item instead of banking, via a single `mendXp` seam read once in `awardXp`.
- **Anvil** (craft: 3 gold ore + 4 cobble) — acts on the selected hotbar gear:
  - **Combine** a duplicate: adds both durability bars + a bonus and **merges enchantments** at the higher level, consuming the duplicate.
  - **Material repair**: consume the item's tier material (diamond ore → diamond sword, cobble → stone pickaxe, …) for a chunk of durability.

content.text:
CodeRabbit posted **9 actionable comments**. I triaged them, applied the valid ones, and committed the fixes locally (not pushed — your call to review first).

## Applied (6)

| Fix | What |
|---|---|
| **save: per-enchant clamp** | `restoreEnchantments` now clamps each enchant to its *own* max, so a tampered `mending:3` save loads as level 1 (was clamped to the global `ENCHANT_MAX_LEVEL` of 3). + regression test. |
| **anvil rename field** | Reset key now includes the saved name (swapping a same-id item with a different name refreshes the field), submit is sanitized, input cap uses `CUSTOM_NAME_MAX_LEN`. |
| **docs/reference** | Fixed the self-contradiction — intro now says "per-enchant max (3 for most, 1 for Mending)" instead of a flat "level 3". |
| **docs/adding-content** | Dedicated-panel guidance now names the grindstone alongside enchanting/anvil. |
| **test type-safety** | New `ench`/`enchanted` helpers use `EnchantmentId` instead of `id as never` (anvil, grindstone, GrindstoneColumn tests). |
| **test constant** | Combine-bonus assertion uses `ANVIL_REPAIR_BONUS_PCT` instead of a hard-coded `0.12`. |

## Declined (3), with rationale

- **"EquippedArmor needs a per-instance key"** (3 comments: InventoryPanel, mendXp, types). This is **pre-existing, not introduced here** — `equippedDefense`, `armorReduction`, and `consumeEquippedArmorDurability` have *always* resolved equipped armor by `findIndex(slot.id === id)`, and per-instance enchantments shipped back in v7. My `mendXp` just follows that established pattern. Fixing it properly means changing the persisted `equippedArmor` shape plus all four armor seams — a cross-cutting refactor that's out of scope for this PR and worth a dedicated follow-up. I noted this in the commit body.
- **`as unknown as GameState` test fixture** — matches the repo-wide test pattern (`fishing.test.ts`, `combat.test.ts`, etc.); a fully-typed `GameState` fixture is disproportionate here.
